thinking_stances_applied.produced: Pressure the interruption after filename publication but before receipt advancement, then cleanup retry. Current migration guards identity and rejects nonempty live WAL; new destination naming must preserve those guards. The plan explicitly requires this; no uncovered contract gap demonstrated.

Use a new versioned graph-consolidation migration kind over the existing coordinator, preserving old receipt interpretation and semantic backup. Completed legacy receipts must not short-circuit the new transition. This matches the plan and is stronger than extending a global legacy artifact allowlist without migration-kind ownership.

Automatic fresh source graph extraction avoids all old-format decoding and corrupt-cache compatibility. Reuse vectors, retain a bounded owned cleanup manifest, and separate paired qualification from destination upgrades. Do not add a bridge release or second shipped engine.

Shared filename alone cannot create atomic publication. One coordinator must own data transaction and final authorization, while a response holds generation-consistent graph/community and semantic inputs. Existing finalizer owns separate FULL-durable and memory authorization machinery; preserving those fences is a required integration seam already covered by the plan.

Treat cutover like a journaled filesystem transaction: the receipt authorizes one candidate identity and records intent before authority changes; restart verification earns cleanup eligibility. Treat resident caches like immutable versioned snapshots, retaining an old generation until in-flight readers finish.

primer.strongest_challenge: The most material pressure point is migration-kind dispatch and authority continuity across existing completed/pending receipts, two database filenames, process restart, and graph cleanup. Current prepare_upgrade returns immediately for a complete receipt (543-544), while cleanup_legacy owns only docs.lance/code.lance/__manifest (24,1142-1145). Merely changing the filename and adding graph tables would either skip the transition or weaken deletion ownership. The plan explicitly addresses both, so this is a challenge for independent lanes to validate, not an actionable plan defect.

best_alternative.approach: Keep the existing coordinator but add a separately versioned consolidation transition: finish a pending legacy receipt according to its original package identity; preserve the historical completed receipt; create a new migration-kind receipt for staged semantic backup plus source graph rebuild; validate a fresh process before deleting individually owned obsolete graph artifacts; retry cleanup independently of rebuilding a verified graph.
best_alternative.why_better: This would be better than broadening legacy cleanup and reusing a completed receipt because each receipt retains one interpretation and deletion scope, and interruption recovery never guesses authority. It is consistent with the admitted design, not a request for another storage architecture.

primer.consequence_of_current_path: If the stated dispatch, final authorization and per-artifact ownership contracts are implemented, no additional demonstrated readiness consequence remains. If integration shortcuts bypass them, upgrades can incorrectly no-op, publish unauthorized mixed state, or delete unrelated graph-folder contents. These are conditional implementation risks, not observed product failures introduced by this unimplemented wave.
